formation.title: The Caliph of the Southern Sea
formation.text:
Three centuries of Islam have remade Mindanao. From Maimbung to Kuta Watu, from the kris-foundries of Lanao to the vinta wharves of the Iranun coast, Sunni faith has bound together what no Spanish, Dutch, or English fleet has ever conquered.

Now the impossible has happened. The rival Sultanates of Sulu and Maguindanao no longer war. The rajahs of Butuan and the datus of Buayan and Zamboanga kneel together. The pandita and ulama have spoken with one voice: Mindanao must speak with one voice as well.

A single oath of fealty awaits. The vinta fleets are at sail. The kalis are unsheathed. The question is what kind of polity this Moro Sultanate will be.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Sultan-Caliph of the Moros

modifiers.name: The Sultan-Caliph of the Moros
modifiers.text: One Sultan, one Caliph, one banner over Mindanao. The ulama swear fealty to a single throne; pandita schools teach the same fiqh from Sulu to Lanao; conversion of pagan and animist datus proceeds under royal sanction. Religious authority and political authority are made one.

options.text: A Confederation of Datus

modifiers.name: A Confederation of Datus
modifiers.text: Power flows upward from the datus, not downward from the Sultan. Each rajah keeps his retainers, each chief his territory; the Caliph is first among equals, not master of all. The cost of unity is paid in centralized authority, but the gain is in the levies of every clan and the loyalty of every datu's house.

options.text: By Sword and by Sail

modifiers.name: By Sword and by Sail
modifiers.text: The vinta fleets sail at the new moon and return laden with plunder. From the Visayan coasts to the Borneo straits, the lantakas roar. War is not the failure of statecraft but its instrument; jihad against the unbeliever is the discipline that holds the Moro nation together.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

advances.name: Foundation of Sharif ul-Hashim
advances.text: The arrival of the Sunni missionary Sharif ul-Hashim at Buansa in 1457 founds the Sultanate of Sulu and binds the warrior nobility of the southern islands to the Hashemite genealogy and Sunni faith.

event.title: The Foundation of Sharif ul-Hashim
event.text:
In the year 1457 of the Christian reckoning, the Johore-born scholar and missionary Sharif ul-Hashim came to Buansa on Jolo and was acclaimed Sultan. He had crossed the seas with the Quran, the chronicles of the Prophet, and the genealogies that traced his line back to the Hashemites. Where the datu-rajah hierarchy had once ruled by ancestry alone, now it ruled by ancestry sanctified through Islam.

The Sharif's first concern is the doctrine itself: which strand of the faith shall the Moro Sultanate plant in its soil? The orthodox jurists of Mecca, with their codified Shafi'i fiqh and their disciplined schools, send their books and their scholars. The Sufi tariqa brotherhoods, with their saints and their popular conversions, send their living teachers. The Sharif must choose.

options.text: Receive the orthodox Shafi'i fiqh from Mecca

modifiers.name: Orthodox Shafi'i Fiqh
modifiers.text: The codified law of Mecca's Shafi'i school is transplanted whole to the southern islands. The qadi cite the same texts read in Cairo and Aceh; the imam preaches the same khutba; literacy in classical Arabic spreads through the ulama corps.

options.text: Plant the Sufi tariqa brotherhoods among the people

modifiers.name: Sufi Tariqa Brotherhoods
modifiers.text: The Naqshbandi, Qadiri and Shadhili brotherhoods plant their saints in every major Moro town. Conversion happens through love rather than the sword, and the old anitist diwata are softened into Sufi pirs rather than denied outright.

advances.name: Kris and Kalis Metallurgy
advances.text: The wavy-bladed kris and longer kalis are forged in the workshops of Mindanao with techniques passed from Java and Sulawesi: pamor patterns hammered from layered iron, blades blessed by panditas, hilts inlaid with silver and ivory.

advances.name: The Datu's Oath
advances.text: The pre-Islamic system of datu, rajah, and timawa is fused with the new Sultanate. Each datu retains his retainers and his lands, but swears fealty to the Sultan-Caliph at the foundation of every reign.

advances.name: The Balangay Seafarers
advances.text: The plank-built balangay, ancestor of the vinta, has crossed the Sulu Sea since before recorded history. Its successors carry Moro warriors to every coast within a thousand leagues of Mindanao.

advances.name: Pandita Schools
advances.text: The pandita teaches Quran and law in his open-walled school. Around him gather the children of datus and slaves alike; from him come the next generation of clerks, judges, and imams of the Moro nation.

event.title: The Pandita and the Ulama
event.text:
In every Moro town now there is a pandita, a man who has studied with the great teachers of Sulu, who has perhaps made the hajj to Mecca, who can read the Arabic of the Quran and write the Tausug of the chronicles. Around him gather children, but the diwan must decide which children.

Some pandita teach all who can sit before them: the slave's son beside the datu's, the freeman beside the rajah's heir. Others reserve the deeper texts for the datu and ulama lines, the future judges and ambassadors of the Sultanate. Both visions promise the same scholarship, but very different societies.

options.text: Open the schools to all: slave and datu's son alike

modifiers.name: Pandita Schools Open to All
modifiers.text: The slave's son sits beside the datu's at the pandita's mat. Talent rises where the throne could not predict; literacy reaches every barangay; the Moro corps of clerks, judges and ambassadors swells from beyond the noble line.

options.text: Reserve them for the datu and ulama lines

modifiers.name: Pandita Schools of the Lineages
modifiers.text: Deep texts and the high jurisprudence are reserved for the datu and ulama lines. The Moro literati form a tighter, more disciplined caste; legitimacy and learning are bound to the noble inheritance.

advances.name: The Vinta Fleets
advances.text: Lateen-rigged outrigger warships armed with deck-mounted lantakas. Faster than any Spanish galleon, harder to catch than any Dutch frigate. The vinta is the cornerstone of Moro maritime power.

event.title: The Vinta and the Lantaka
event.text:
The boats are everywhere now: outrigger hulls of nara wood, lateen sails painted in the okir patterns of Sulu, deck-mounted lantakas of bronze cast at Maguindanao foundries. They are smaller than the Spanish galleons, smaller even than the Brunei perahus, but they are faster than both, and they cluster like wasps.

The debate in the Sultan's diwan is sharp. The Iranun datus want letters of marque, raids on the Visayan coast, slaves and plunder for the warrior nobility. The royal admiralty wants a regular fleet, prahus organized into squadrons, lantakas standardized, the Sulu Sea made a Moro lake. Both visions promise the same vinta, but very different uses for it.

options.text: Loose the Iranun corsairs upon the Visayas.

modifiers.name: The Iranun Corsairs
modifiers.text: The Iranun raid by moonlight in fleets of forty vintas, ranging from the Visayas to the Strait of Malacca. They take slaves, silver, weapons, and reputation. The Spanish call it piracy; the Moros call it war.

options.text: Build a royal admiralty for the Sulu Sea.

modifiers.name: The Royal Admiralty
modifiers.text: The Sultan's shipwrights work in standardized yards. Vinta hulls are measured to a single template, lantakas cast to a single bore. The Sulu Sea becomes a disciplined sea, patrolled in squadrons under the green banner.

advances.name: Kalis Warriors
advances.text: The wavy-bladed kalis is wielded by every Moro warrior of standing. In boarding actions and forest skirmishes alike, its serpentine edge inflicts wounds that resist healing.

advances.name: The Iranun Raiders
advances.text: The Iranun datus of the Illana Bay have raided since the Spaniards first set foot on Cebu. Their fleets range from Borneo to the Visayas, taking slaves, plunder, and reputation.

advances.name: Kuta Stockades
advances.text: The kuta is a ringed wooden stockade defended by lantakas, ditches, and bamboo spikes. Kuta Watu and dozens like it have stood against Spanish artillery for centuries.

advances.name: The Reign of Sultan Kudarat
advances.text: Muhammad Dipatuan Kudarat (r. 1619-71), the greatest sultan Mindanao has ever produced, ruler of nine modern provinces, defender of the southern islands, the man whose name is still invoked when the Moro speak of resistance.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

event.title: Sultan Kudarat and the Long Defiance
event.text:
He is the greatest sultan Mindanao has ever produced: Muhammad Dipatuan Kudarat, descendant of Sharif Kabungsuwan, ruler of nine modern provinces, the man who turned back the Spanish at Lamitan in 1637 with two thousand juramentado warriors and held them off for thirty more years.

His reign is the golden age of Maguindanao. His diwan receives ambassadors from Brunei, Aceh, and the Dutch. His vinta fleets dominate the Sulu Sea. His name is spoken in the same breath as Suleiman the Magnificent and Akbar the Great.

Now Kudarat sends word: the Spanish have asked for terms. The choice is his to make, and his Sultanate's character will be decided by it.

options.text: Press the jihad of Lamitan to the gates of Manila.

modifiers.name: The Jihad of Lamitan
modifiers.text: Two thousand juramentado, sworn before Allah to die for the faith, march under the Moro banner. The kalis are unsheathed; the kampilans flash; the vinta fleets blockade the Spanish ports. War, not peace, is the language of the Sultan-Caliph.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

options.text: Sign the Peace of Atienza and reopen the harbours.

modifiers.name: The Peace of Atienza
modifiers.text: In 1645 the treaty is signed. The Sultan opens his harbours; Maguindanao trade flourishes. Pearls, tortoise-shell, slaves, beeswax, and rice flow through Cotabato to Manila and Macao. Kudarat's golden age is born of restraint, not war.

advances.name: Lantaka Foundries
advances.text: Bronze swivel guns cast in Maguindanao and Sulu workshops. The lantaka arms every vinta and kuta, and serves as currency in inter-datu marriages and tributes.

advances.name: The Sulu-Brunei Axis
advances.text: Royal marriages bind Sulu, Maguindanao, and Brunei into a single Islamic dynastic web stretching from northern Borneo to Mindanao. Tribute, trade, and shared genealogies hold the alliance together.

advances.name: The Sultan's Diwan
advances.text: The Sultan-Caliph receives datus, ambassadors, panditas, and ulama in a court patterned on the great diwans of the Islamic world. Decrees are recorded in Arabic and Tausug; embassies arrive from Aceh, Brunei, and the Mughal coast.

advances.name: Pansacan Corsair Fleets
advances.text: Organized squadrons of vintas under the Iranun and Samal datus dominate the Celebes Sea. They blockade Spanish ports, intercept Dutch shipping, and turn the strait between Mindanao and Borneo into a Moro highway.

advances.name: The Kampilan Bearers
advances.text: The two-handed kampilan, sword of the Maguindanao golden age, is wielded by elite shock troops in the Sultan's standing companies. Its weight crushes through helmets; its length keeps Spanish pikemen at bay.

advances.name: The Sulu Pearl Trade
advances.text: The pearl banks of Tawi-Tawi and Jolo yield gems that reach Beijing, Mecca, and Amsterdam. Sulu pearls are an instrument of Moro diplomacy and the fortune of the Tausug datus.

advances.name: The Madrasah Network
advances.text: Stone-walled madrasahs in every major Moro town teach Arabic, fiqh, and the chronicles of Islam. Graduates serve as judges, ambassadors, and panditas across the southern islands.

advances.name: Garay Corsair Warships
advances.text: The garay is the great Iranun raid warship of the late Sulu Zone, larger than the vinta, carrying a dozen lantakas, oar-driven for windless conditions, designed for plunder and prisoner-taking on the great seasonal raids.

advances.name: The Way of the Juramentado
advances.text: The juramentado has sworn before the imam to die in jihad. He attacks alone or in small bands, kalis in hand, knowing he will not return. He is the answer of the Moro people to three centuries of colonial war.

event.title: The Way of the Juramentado
event.text:
He has shaved his head, bound his loins, and taken the oath before the imam: he will go forth alone or in small bands, kalis in hand, and he will not return. He believes that to fall in jihad is to enter Paradise; he believes that the colonizer's bullets cannot take from him what Allah has not willed.

The Spanish call him 'juramentado': 'one who has sworn.' They do not understand him, and they fear him.

The Sultan's diwan must decide what the throne's relation to him shall be. Sanction the juramentado as a Sultan-licensed warrior order, with imams sworn to the throne and a discipline that flows from the diwan. Or let him fight as folk resistance, beyond the throne, sworn only to Allah and his village's imam.

options.text: Sanction them as a Sultan-licensed warrior order

modifiers.name: Sultan-Sworn Juramentado
modifiers.text: The juramentado are sworn before the Sultan's imam, drilled in the kuta, and led by Sultan-appointed captains. Their oath binds them to throne and faith together; the diwan controls when they march.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

options.text: Let them fight as folk resistance, beyond the throne

modifiers.name: Folk Juramentado of the Villages
modifiers.text: The juramentado swears before his village imam, beyond the throne's writ. The Sultan does not order him; the village does. Where the kuta falls and the diwan is silenced, the folk juramentado walks alone into the colonizer's camp, and the war goes on.

advances.name: Cotta Stone Fortresses
advances.text: The cotta is the great stone fortress of the late Moro wars: walled, banner-flying, lantaka-armed citadels where the Sultan's banner flies long after the colonizer thinks the war is won.

advances.name: Tawi-Tawi Pearl Diveries
advances.text: Organized diving fleets of Sama-Bajau and Tausug divers harvest the great pearl banks. Their work, dangerous and underpaid, fuels the wealth of the late Sultanate and feeds the Sulu Zone economy.

advances.name: The Sulu Zone Economy
advances.text: At its height the Sulu Zone is the largest slaving and raiding economy in maritime Southeast Asia. Vinta and garay fleets harvest captives, pearls, and forest products from a thousand miles of coast and trade them to Canton, Batavia, and Manila.

advances.name: The Long Jihad
advances.text: Three centuries of colonial war have not broken the Moro. They fight on, in the kuta, in the cotta, in the back-country, in the jungle, in the way of the juramentado. The colonizer's empire rises and falls; the green banner remains.

advances.name: Pan-Moro Unity
advances.text: Tausug, Maguindanao, Iranun, Maranao, Sama-Bajau, and Yakan recognize themselves as one people, the Bangsa Moro, bound by faith, by the kalis, by the vinta, and by three centuries of shared resistance.

advances.name: Steam-Powered Corsairs
advances.text: The Moro shipwrights of Sandakan and Maimbung adopt the small steam launch as a successor to the vinta. Steam-driven raid craft, faster than any sail, harder to escape than any oared garay, carry the long jihad into the age of coal.

advances.name: The Bangsa Moro
advances.text: Tausug, Maguindanao, Maranao, Iranun, Sama-Bajau, Yakan, Sangil, Jama Mapun, Kalagan, Kalibugan, Palawani, Molbog, and Sangir all recognize themselves as one nation: the Bangsa Moro, the Moro people, the southern alternative to colonial imposition that has lasted three centuries and will not break.

destiny.name: The Banner of the Sultan-Caliph
destiny.text:
The Moro polity is proclaimed: one Sultan, one banner, one ummah from Sulu to Surigao. The pandita read the khutba in the Sultan's name; the datus kiss the green flag at every harbour. The destiny of the Bangsa Moro is now to be chosen.

Requires: 25 stability.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Banner Unfurled
event.text:
On the steps of the Sultan's diwan, the green banner of the Moros is unfurled before the assembled datus, panditas, ulama, and ambassadors of the southern islands. The shahada is recited; the kris are kissed; the Sultan's name is proclaimed in the friday khutba from Maimbung to Lake Lanao.

The path of the Moro nation is now in the Sultan's hand, and the destiny of the Bangsa Moro is open to choose.

options.text: The banner has been raised.

destiny.name: The Juramentado Corps
destiny.text:
Standing companies of jurat-sworn warriors are raised and trained from boyhood. The kris is unsheathed in the Visayas; the Sulu vinta strikes at the Brunei coast. The southern islands learn the cost of crossing the Moro nation.

Requires: Sword and Sail destiny path; own Cebu (Singhapala); own Brunei (Berune); a Kris Foundry in 2 locations.

conditions.text: Sword and Sail path: maritime jihad.
Own Singhapala, or a subject owns it
Own Berune, or a subject owns it
A Kris Foundry stands in at least 2 of our locations

event.title: The Juramentado Corps
event.text:
In the courtyard of the great kuta of Maimbung, the imam binds the loins of the first hundred. They have shaved their heads, made the wudu, and sworn before Allah and the Sultan to die in jihad rather than break ranks.

The diwan debates the corps's mission. Some demand a kris brotherhood drilled for the close-quarters shock that broke the Spanish at Lamitan. Others demand vinta corsair-juramentado, sworn to die in the boarding action against the colonial galleons. The Sultan's hand will weight the doctrine.

options.text: Train the kris brotherhood: close-quarters shock

modifiers.name: Kris Brotherhood Drilled
modifiers.text: Standing companies of kris- and kampilan-bearers train daily in the kuta courtyards. The wave-bladed close-quarters shock that broke Spanish lines at Lamitan is now a permanent doctrine of the Moro army.

options.text: Train the vinta corsair-juramentado: naval boarding

modifiers.name: Vinta Corsair-Juramentado
modifiers.text: The juramentado are taught the boarding action: kalis in hand, the leap from the lateen-rigged vinta onto the Spanish galleon's deck, the prayer recited as the colonial bullets begin. A naval doctrine of the willing dead.

destiny.name: The Lantaka Armada
destiny.text:
The vinta and garay fleets patrol from Maluku to Sabah. Lantaka batteries close the Sulu and Celebes seas to colonial shipping. The Sultan-Caliph's banner flies over the spice approaches.

Requires: Own Ternate; own Brunei (Api Api); own Sandakan; a Lantaka Foundry in 2 locations.

conditions.text: Own Ternate, or a subject owns it
Own Api Api, or a subject owns it
Own Sandakan, or a subject owns it
A Lantaka Foundry stands in at least 2 of our locations

event.title: The Armada Takes the Inland Seas
event.text:
From the foundries of Maguindanao the lantakas come down by the hundreds. From the wharves of Sulu the vinta squadrons sail in fleets of forty. The Spanish galleon and the Dutch frigate are turned back at Ternate; the Brunei perahu falls in line at Sandakan. The southern seas are a Moro lake.

The Sultan's diwan debates the use to which this armada should be put. The Iranun datus call for the great raid: a generation of plunder reaching to Mindoro and Borneo's western coast. The royal admiralty calls for the great blockade: the closing of the Maluku spice approaches against every European flag.

options.text: Loose the Iranun corsairs upon the Visayas and Borneo.

modifiers.name: The Iranun Armada
modifiers.text: The corsair fleets range from Mindoro to Borneo, taking slaves, silver, and reputation. Moro warbands move with the tides, supplied by raid and tribute, and earn fame in every campaign.

options.text: Close the Maluku approaches in royal blockade.

modifiers.name: The Maluku Blockade
modifiers.text: Pearls and spice flow into the Sultan's coffers as the European companies are turned away from Ternate. The blockade enriches the treasury and bends the great powers to the negotiating table, though the masons and carpenters of the home islands are pulled to the war yards.

destiny.name: The Caliphate of the Southern Seas
destiny.text:
Manila has fallen. Tondo prays five times a day. Gowa kneels to the Sultan-Caliph. The colonial age has been answered with sword and sail, and the southern seas are a Moro lake at last. Unlocks the Juramentado Brotherhood.

Requires: Own Maynila; own Tondo; own Gowa; 3000 gold.

conditions.text: Own Maynila, or a subject owns it
Own Tondo, or a subject owns it
Own Gowa, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Caliphate of the Southern Seas
event.text:
Manila has fallen to the kalis. Tondo's bells are silent; the friday khutba is read from the cathedral pulpit of the conquistadors. Gowa kneels. Brunei renews her oath. The Sultan-Caliph of the Moros is master of every shore from Sulawesi to Luzon.

The diwan now considers the form this dominion shall take. Some say the Moro nation must become a true caliphate: a state of war and sharia, of disciplined corps and conquering armies, that shall not stop until every island flies the green banner. Others say the dominion is already won, and that the future lies in the ordered economy of the Sulu Zone: a maritime imperium of pearls, slaves, and tributary trade.

options.text: Forge a true caliphate of sword and sharia.

modifiers.name: The Southern Caliphate
modifiers.text: The Moro caliphate marches in disciplined corps. The military tactics of the kalis and kampilan are codified in the Sultan's manual; the besieger learns the kuta's ditch and the cotta's stone wall. The civil hand of the state is light, for the sword is the law.

options.text: Master the Sulu Zone economy at its peak.

modifiers.name: The Sulu Zone at Peak
modifiers.text: Pearl, slave, beeswax, and forest product flow through the Sulu Zone in volumes never seen before. The treasury fills; the moneylenders of Canton offer their best rates. The southern islands grow rich on raid and trade, but the conscience of the Muslim world looks askance at the chained captives in Jolo's market.

destiny.name: The Codification of Sharia
destiny.text:
The qadi assemble in the Sultan's diwan. The fiqh of the southern islands is set down in writing for the first time, drawn from Shafi'i jurisprudence and Tausug custom alike. The age of written law in the Moro polity begins.

Requires: Sultan-Caliph destiny path; a madrasa in two of our towns; 1000 gold; 50 prestige.

conditions.text: Sultan-Caliph path: centralized Islamic monarchy.
A Madrasa or Mosque-Madrasah stands in at least 2 of our locations
Gold at least 1000
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Codification of Sharia
event.text:
The qadi gather under the Sultan's banner: scholars from Sulu, Maguindanao, Buayan, and Lake Lanao, each bringing his chronicles, his Shafi'i texts, and his customary law. For a year they argue.

The deeper question is theirs to settle: shall the new fiqh be pure Shafi'i orthodoxy, transplanted whole from the schools of Mecca, that the Moro nation may speak the same legal language as the wider ummah? Or shall it be a hybrid code that weaves the Quran and the Shafi'i school together with the customs of the datu, a Moro sharia answerable only to itself?

options.text: Pure Shafi'i orthodoxy from Mecca

modifiers.name: Shafi'i Orthodoxy
modifiers.text: The new fiqh is pure Shafi'i, transplanted whole from Mecca. The Moro nation now speaks the same legal language as the wider ummah; the qadi cite the same texts in Sulu as in Cairo and Aceh.

effects.name: Invite Religious Figure from Same School Cost

options.text: A hybrid code blending Shafi'i with Tausug custom

modifiers.name: Moro Sharia Code
modifiers.text: The new fiqh weaves the Quran and the Shafi'i school together with the customs of the datu. The Moro nation has its own sharia, answerable only to itself; legitimacy flows from the law as much as from the throne.

destiny.name: The Pan-Islamic Trade Network
destiny.text:
Moro pearl, beeswax, and tortoise-shell reach Aceh, Malacca, and Temasek. The Sultan's writ runs from the Sulu Sea to the Strait of Malacca, binding the Islamic trade circuits of maritime Southeast Asia under one banner.

Requires: Own Malacca; own Bandar Aceh; own Temasek; 2000 gold.

conditions.text: Own Malacca, or a subject owns it
Own Bandar Aceh, or a subject owns it
Own Temasek, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Pan-Islamic Network
event.text:
Moro pearl reaches Mecca. Moro beeswax reaches Hadhramaut. Moro pilgrims, robed in the white ihram, walk the haram with hajjis from Aceh, Bengal, and the Mughal coast. The southern islands have entered the Indian Ocean Islamic world as full members.

The Sultan must choose how this network will be ordered. The merchant party calls for a hajj caravan system: direct overland and overseas pilgrim routes, secured by tribute and treaty, drawing the wealth of the ummah through Maguindanao. The diplomatic party calls for a great compact with Aceh and Brunei: a confederation of Sunni sultanates that shall stand against every Christian and Hindu power in the eastern seas.

options.text: Build the hajj caravans through Maguindanao.

modifiers.name: The Hajj Caravans
modifiers.text: Pilgrim convoys move from Cotabato to Mecca and back along secured routes. Moro merchants ride with them; Moro coin is recognized in Aden and Surat; the Sultan's name is welcomed at every port of the ummah.

options.text: Sign the Aceh-Sulu-Brunei compact.

modifiers.name: The Aceh Compact
modifiers.text: Aceh, Sulu, Brunei, and Maguindanao stand bound by a single compact: shared embassies, shared spies, shared shipwrights. No Christian power moves in the eastern seas without the Sultan-Caliph hearing of it.

destiny.name: The Civilization of the Pandita
destiny.text:
The southern islands have become a beacon of Sunni civilization. Madrasahs in every town, qadi in every diwan, ulama trained in Mecca returning to teach in Cotabato and Jolo. From Palembang of Sumatra to Demak of Java, the great Islamic seats of maritime Asia answer to one Caliph.

Requires: Own Palembang; own Demak; 75 prestige; 3000 gold. Unlocks the Grand Mosque.

conditions.text: Own Palembang, or a subject owns it
Own Demak, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Civilization of the Pandita
event.text:
The southern islands have become an Islamic civilization in their own right. Madrasahs stand in every town. The fiqh is taught in Tausug and Maguindanao Arabic alike. Pandita-judges arbitrate every dispute from Sandakan to Cebu. Pilgrims from Java and Brunei come north to study at Cotabato and Jolo.

Now the Sultan-Caliph's diwan considers the apex of this civilization. Some hold that the future lies with the tariqa: the Sufi brotherhoods that have penetrated even the most remote barrios, binding the Bangsa Moro through love and song. Others hold that the future lies with the legalists: a Sultan-Solomon, ruling the southern seas in justice and order, the equal of any caliph in Islamic memory.

options.text: Empower the tariqa Sufi brotherhoods.

modifiers.name: The Tariqa Brotherhoods
modifiers.text: Sufi orders penetrate every village. The dhikr is sung at every haflah; conversion proceeds not by sword but by song. The Bangsa Moro embraces a wider Islam, accommodating local custom, though the legalist ulama complain of doctrinal looseness.

options.text: Reign as Sultan-Solomon, the legalist apex.

modifiers.name: Sultan-Solomon
modifiers.text: The Sultan rules with the wisdom of Sulayman: every petition heard, every law enforced, every datu disciplined. The southern islands are governed as a single ordered realm. The civil discipline draws away from the martial; the kuta walls grow thinner as the diwan halls grow grander.

units.name: Vinta
units.text: Lateen-rigged outrigger warship armed with deck-mounted lantakas. Faster than any Spanish galleon, harder to catch than any Dutch frigate, the cornerstone of Moro maritime power.

units.name: Garay
units.text: Great Iranun raid warship of the late Sulu Zone: larger than the vinta, oar-driven for windless conditions, carrying a dozen lantakas and a boarding party of kalis warriors.

units.name: Balangay Warriors
units.text: Coastal levy raised for raids and shore defense: crews of the balangay, ancestor of the vinta, who fight on land as well as at sea.

units.name: Kalis Warriors
units.text: Moro warrior-nobles bearing the wavy-bladed kalis. In melee and on boarding actions their blades inflict wounds that resist healing. The kalis is feared across maritime Southeast Asia.

units.name: Kampilan Bearers
units.text: Elite shock infantry wielding the two-handed kampilan, sword of the Maguindanao golden age. The kampilan crushes through helmets and clears the line for the kris-bearers behind.

units.name: Iranun Raiders
units.text: Coastal pirate-warriors of Illana Bay: crews of vinta and garay who fight equally well as land levies, fast across coastal terrain and devastating on plunder raids.

buildings.name: Kris Foundry
buildings.text: Traditional smithing workshop where layered iron is hammered into the wavy-bladed kris and longer kalis. Each blade carries the pamor pattern of its smith and the blessings of the pandita.

buildings.name: Kuta
buildings.text: Ringed wooden stockade defended by lantakas, ditches, and bamboo spikes. The kuta is the workhorse fortification of the southern islands: cheaper than stone, faster to build, and remarkably resistant to colonial artillery in tropical terrain.

buildings.name: Lantaka Foundry
buildings.text: Bronze foundry casting the lantaka swivel-gun. Lantakas arm every vinta and every kuta, and serve as currency, dowry, and tribute among the datus.

buildings.name: Sultan's Diwan
buildings.text: The court of the Sultan-Caliph, patterned on the great diwans of the Islamic world. Datus, ambassadors, panditas, and ulama gather here; decrees are recorded in Arabic and Tausug.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: Mosque-Madrasah
buildings.text: Stone-walled mosque and Quranic school in one. Children of datu and slave alike learn Arabic, fiqh, and the chronicles of Islam under the pandita's tutelage.

buildings.name: Cotta
buildings.text: Great stone fortress of the late Moro wars: walled, banner-flying, lantaka-armed. Where the kuta defies the colonizer's artillery, the cotta defies his armies.

buildings.name: Pearl Divers' Camp
buildings.text: Organized diving fleet of Sama-Bajau and Tausug divers working the pearl banks of Tawi-Tawi, Jolo, and the Sulu Archipelago.

where.text: Pearls is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Juramentado Brotherhood
buildings.text: Permanent chapterhouse of the jurat-sworn warriors. Boys are taken in young, trained for a decade in kalis and kampilan, and bound by oath to die before retreat. The brotherhood is the standing arm of the Sultan-Caliph and the terror of every colonial garrison.
buildings.unlocked_by: The Caliphate of the Southern Seas

buildings.name: Grand Mosque
buildings.text: The great congregational mosque of the southern islands. Its minaret rises over the Sultan's diwan; its mihrab points to Mecca; its friday khutba binds the Bangsa Moro into one ummah under one Sultan-Caliph.

list.name: Ruma Bichara
list.text: The advisory state council of the Sulu Sultanate (its Maguindanao counterpart called Bichara Atas), composed of the leading datus and resident sharifs. The Datu Raja Muda, Datu Maharaja Adenduk, Datu Ladja Laut, and other titled officers met in council; each held one vote, the Sultan two, and the Raja Muda two. Beyond advising, the Ruma Bichara elected the Sultan's heir-apparent from the male-line, which made it impossible for any sultan to disregard.

list.name: Pandita Madrasah Network
list.text: Islamic education organised through the houses of the pandita (Sanskrit-derived 'learned man') and the masjid, established across Mindanao and Sulu from the late thirteenth century onward by Arab missionaries. Every datu maintained his own pandita as religious advisor; together they constituted the Bangsa Moro ulama. Quranic instruction was conducted in pandita homes and mosques, producing the literate clerks the Sultan's chancery needed and policing the doctrinal cohesion that backed the Sultan-Caliph claim.

conditions.text: Sunnism religion

list.name: Tarsila Chancery
list.text: The keepers of the tarsila (from Arabic silsilah, 'chain'), the written genealogical records that traced the Sulu Sultans to Sayyid Abu Bakr and through him to the Prophet. Every leading datu kept his own tarsila; the Sultan's chancery curated the official lineages, validated rival claims, and arbitrated marriage alliances. Without these scrolls a claimant was just another raja; with them, he was the Caliph of the Southern Sea.

list.name: Panglima District Administration
list.text: The provincial reach of the Sultanate, organised under district panglima (the equivalent of mayors) who in turn governed barrio captains variously titled maharaja, orangkaya, and parukka. The panglima collected zakat and tribute, administered justice in the Sultan's name, and translated central edicts into local enforcement. When the offices became hereditary, however, panglima titles passed by inheritance and the barrio captains skimmed at every level.

list.name: Parang Sabil Brotherhood
list.text: The institution of the mag-sabil (Tausug: 'one who endures the pangs of death'), Moro warriors who took the Napi oath to die in the path of God against unbelievers. Candidates required parental consent and the Sultan's personal authorisation before being entrusted to imams for spiritual and martial preparation. The mag-sabil drew kris and barong against Spanish garrisons in attacks the Spanish themselves coined as 'juramentado' in 1876. When licensed by the Sultan it was the realm's most feared deterrent; when not, it became uncontrolled vendetta.

list.name: Lanong Corsair Admiralty
list.text: The naval establishment under the Datu Ladja Laut, which from roughly 1770 to 1870 launched between one and two hundred Iranun and Banguingui warships every year out of Maimbung, Malabang, and the Iranun coast. The lanong was a thirty-metre outrigger with up to three banks of oars and lantaka swivel-guns; the lighter garay raided faster. Captives sold at the Jolo and Tawi-Tawi markets supplied the labour force on which the Sultanate's economy substantially depended. By the 1850s Bisaya captives may have made up half the population of Sulu.
